q: What does regulatory compliance mean for a business?
r: Following the laws and regulations that apply to its operations
Compliance means meeting legal and regulatory requirements.
w: Industry standards are set by organizations and regulators, not by compliance alone.
Compliance does not mean avoiding oversight.
Choosing the cheapest legal option every time
Cost is a factor but not the definition of compliance.

q: A health inspector finds a restaurant storing food at unsafe temperatures. This violation falls mainly under which type of compliance?
r: Health and safety regulations
Food storage rules protect public health.
w: Tax rules cover reporting and paying taxes.
These cover how products may be promoted.
These cover whether workers are employees or contractors.

q: Which U.S. agency sets and enforces workplace safety standards?
r: Occupational Safety and Health Administration
OSHA enforces safety and health standards for workplaces.
w: The FTC handles consumer protection and competition.

q: An employer must keep records of employee hours and pay for several years. What is the main reason?
r: To prove compliance with wage and hour laws in an audit or dispute
Records are the evidence regulators and courts look for.
w: To set next year's product prices
Pricing does not depend on payroll retention rules.
Advertising rules do not require payroll records.

q: What is the main responsibility of a company's compliance officer?
r: Making sure policies and operations follow laws and regulations
The role exists to monitor and reduce legal and regulatory risk.
w: Sales targets belong to sales management.
Packaging is a product design function.

q: Which is a likely result of failing to comply with applicable regulations?
r: Fines or other legal penalties
Regulators can fine businesses and require them to correct violations.
w: Violations do not reduce tax bills.
Violations can put licenses at risk.

q: Which feature separates a project from everyday operations?
r: It has a defined beginning and end
Projects are temporary efforts aimed at a specific result.
w: Projects exist to reach a defined goal.
Every project needs people, time or money.

q: A project manager lists tasks, owners and due dates on a chart. What is this tool mainly used for?
r: Scheduling work and tracking progress
A schedule shows who does what and by when.
w: Recruiting uses job postings and interviews.

q: What is the scope of a project?
r: The work that is included in, and left out of, the project
Scope sets the boundaries of what the project will deliver.
w: The pay of the team members
Pay is part of the budget.
The number of customers served after launch
This is an outcome, not the project's boundaries.
The legal structure of the company
This is unrelated to project scope.

q: Halfway through a website project the client asks for three new features. What should the project manager do first?
r: Assess the effect on time and cost and agree any changes before proceeding
Managing scope change protects the schedule and budget.
w: Add the features without telling anyone
Refuse all changes regardless of their value
Some changes may be worth making.
Pause the project until the client leaves
This does not resolve the request.

q: Which two are among the classic constraints on a project?
r: Time and cost
Projects are limited by schedule and budget, along with scope.
w: These are product features, not project constraints.

q: What does a project risk register list?
r: Possible problems, how likely they are and planned responses
It helps the team prepare before issues occur.
w: The final results of the project
Results appear after the work is done.
Only the contact details of suppliers
Contact lists are not a risk record.

q: Knowledge management is the practice of:
r: Capturing and sharing what an organization knows
It helps people reuse what the organization has learned.

q: Which is an example of tacit knowledge?
r: A veteran technician's instinct for diagnosing a fault
Tacit knowledge lives in experience and is hard to write down.

q: Which tool best helps employees find answers to common questions without asking a coworker?
r: An internal searchable knowledge base
A knowledge base stores answers where anyone can find them.
w: A time sheet records hours worked.
Annual reports are for investors and the public.
An invoice is a billing document.

q: A senior employee will retire soon. Which step best preserves their knowledge before they leave?
r: Document key processes and pair them with a successor
Documentation plus mentoring transfers both explicit and tacit knowledge.
w: Rely on their old email archive alone
An archive does not capture how and why things were done.
Ask them to keep working without pay
This is not a fair or lasting solution.
Delete their old files to save space

q: Which benefit is most closely tied to sharing knowledge across a company?
r: Fewer repeated mistakes
People can learn from earlier experience.
w: Rent is unrelated to knowledge sharing.
Inventory levels do not depend on knowledge sharing.

q: What is quality control?
r: Checking products or services against set standards
Inspection and testing catch problems before customers do.

q: A factory counts the defective items found per 1,000 produced. What is this measure called?
r: Defect rate
The defect rate shows how often the process produces bad items.
w: This shows how quickly stock sells.
This shows how many workers leave.
This compares profit with money invested.

q: What does continuous improvement mean?
r: Making ongoing small changes to improve processes
Steady, regular improvements add up over time.
w: Replacing the whole business every year
That is the opposite of improvement.
Changing only when customers complain loudly
Improvement should be planned, not only reactive.

q: A restaurant uses a checklist each shift to confirm food temperatures and cleanliness. This is an example of:
r: A quality assurance process
Routine checks help prevent problems before they reach customers.

q: Who is the most important judge of a product's quality?
r: The customer
Quality is ultimately defined by whether the customer's needs are met.
w: Competitors do not define a product's quality for buyers.
Accountants track money, not customer satisfaction.

q: Buying an insurance policy is an example of which risk response?
r: Transferring risk
Insurance moves financial loss to the insurer in exchange for premiums.
w: Avoidance means not doing the risky activity.
Buying a policy is a deliberate response.
Insurance reduces exposure to large losses.

q: A shop installs a security system and trains staff to prevent theft. This is mainly risk:
r: Reduction
The shop is lowering the chance and impact of theft.
w: Nothing is being moved to another party.
The shop is acting rather than just accepting the risk.
The shop continues operating and is not removing the risk.

q: Which is an example of speculative risk?
r: Investing in a new product that may earn a profit or lose money
Speculative risk can result in gain or loss.
w: A fire can only cause loss.
An accident can only cause loss.
A flood can only cause loss.

q: A company decides not to sell a product line because of serious safety concerns. Which risk strategy is this?
r: Avoidance
The company removes the risk by not engaging in the activity.
w: Reduction would keep selling while lowering the risk.
Transfer would shift the loss to another party.
Retention would accept the risk and keep selling.

q: What is the first step in the risk management process?
r: Identify possible risks
Risks must be found before they can be assessed or handled.
w: Insurance is a response chosen after assessing risks.
Claims come later, if losses occur.
Reporting is not the first step.

q: What is a ledger?
r: A record of a business's accounts and transactions
A ledger organizes transactions by account.
w: A ledger is a record, not a loan.
Tax forms are filed with tax authorities.
A ledger is a financial record.

q: Which statement of the accounting equation is correct?
r: Assets = Liabilities + Owner's equity
Everything a business owns is financed by debt or by owners.
w: Liabilities belong on the same side as equity.
This mixes income statement and balance sheet items.

q: A business records a sale when it is earned, even if the customer pays later. Which accounting method is this?
r: Accrual accounting
Accrual accounting records revenue when earned and expenses when incurred.
w: Cash basis records transactions only when cash changes hands.
This is not a standard method of recording sales.
This analyzes the cost of producing goods.

q: A business receives a $1,200 supplier invoice that it has not yet paid. How should it be recorded?
r: As an increase in accounts payable
Money owed to suppliers is a liability.
w: As an increase in accounts receivable
An unpaid bill does not reduce expenses.

q: Which type of software do small companies most often use to record daily financial transactions?
r: Accounting software
It records and organizes transactions and produces reports.

q: Why do businesses reconcile their bank statements?
r: To match their records to the bank's and find errors
Reconciliation catches mistakes, missing entries and fraud.
w: To raise their credit score automatically
Reconciling does not affect a credit score.
To reduce the taxes they owe
Reconciliation does not change tax owed.
Interest depends on the account terms.

q: Which is the correct order of the first steps in the accounting cycle?
r: Analyze transactions, journalize them, post to the ledger
Transactions are analyzed, recorded in a journal, then posted to accounts.
w: Post to the ledger, analyze transactions, journalize
Journalize, close the books, analyze transactions
Closing the books comes near the end.
Close the books, post to the ledger, journalize
